script.text: Hundreds of thousands lost power in Ukraine overnight. Is Trump's energy truce over?

President Zelenskyy says Russia hit power infrastructure in four regions overnight, cutting electricity to hundreds of thousands of households. Ukraine's air force says it shot down 371 of 433 long-range drones Russia launched since Saturday evening.

Russia's Defense Ministry says it downed 235 Ukrainian drones overnight. Nizhny Novgorod's governor, Gleb Nikitin, says an industrial site was hit and more than 100 drones were destroyed. Zelenskyy says Ukraine struck a missile plant in Rostov.

Trump said on October eleventh that both sides agreed to an energy ceasefire. Russia has not confirmed that. On Friday, Moscow accused Kyiv of resuming refinery strikes despite a request from Trump to stop.
Will Russia and Ukraine stop energy strikes before winter? Yes or no?

upload.title: Ukraine Loses Power Again. Is the Energy Truce Dead? #shorts
upload.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia struck power infrastructure in four Ukrainian regions overnight on November 1, cutting electricity to hundreds of thousands of households. Ukraine's air force says it shot down 371 of 433 long-range drones launched by Russia since Saturday evening. Russia's Defense Ministry says it downed 235 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight; Nizhny Novgorod Governor Gleb Nikitin says an industrial site was damaged in a large drone attack and more than 100 drones were destroyed, without naming the facility. Kyiv had not claimed that attack. Zelenskyy says Ukraine also hit a plant in Russia's Rostov region that makes missiles. President Donald Trump said on October 11 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire; Russia has not confirmed an agreement. On Friday, Moscow accused Kyiv of resuming refinery strikes despite a request from Trump to stop. Most details come from the warring parties and could not be independently verified.

Sources:
